issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for the animal classes (Seal, Pig, Goat). The template's Main.java example (commented) constructs Seal, Pig, and Goat with two parameters (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")) while the provided solution implements single-parameter constructors that accept only the name (Seal(String name), Pig(String name), Goat(String name)). The problem statement/UML imply animals have only a name attribute and tasks ask to implement constructors that initialize the class attributes. This discrepancy can confuse students about how many constructor parameters to implement and whether an additional attribute (e.g. habitat/type) is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template examples consistent with the UML and solution by changing the commented constructor calls in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). If two-argument constructors are intended instead, update the problem statement/UML and the solution implementation to include and document the additional attribute(s) and add matching constructors in the solution and template.

issues.description: Constructor-parameter concept mismatch: The template's example usage instantiates animals with two-argument constructors (Seal("Clarabelle", "marine"), Pig("Doodle", "domestic"), Goat("Buttinsky", "mountain")) while the problem statement and UML describe animals with only a name attribute (one constructor parameter). The provided solution implementation also defines single-parameter constructors (Seal(String), Pig(String), Goat(String)). A student reading the template example may try to implement two-parameter constructors or be unsure which constructor signature is required, blocking mapping from requirement to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent. Preferred fix: update the example in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to call single-argument constructors matching the UML and solution (Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternative (only if intended): update the problem statement UML and the solution implementations to include the additional attribute and two-parameter constructors, and adjust all examples accordingly.
